literal: Like one who lacks clarity seeing the ultimate truth, if examined, is the virtue performed by one who lacks compassion.
translation: If one considers it, the virtuous deeds performed by a person devoid of compassion are like a man of confused mind attempting to perceive the ultimate truth.
modern: ஆராய்ந்து பார்த்தால், அருள் இல்லாதவன் செய்யும் அறச்செயலானது, மனத்தெளிவு இல்லாதவன் மெய்ப்பொருளைக் கண்டதைப் போன்றதாகும்.
explanation: This couplet compares the virtue practiced by someone without compassion to a confused person trying to perceive the ultimate truth. Just as a person lacking mental clarity cannot truly comprehend or sustain the realization of ultimate reality, a person who lacks basic compassion cannot perform genuine, lasting acts of virtue. Compassion is the very foundation of virtue; without it, any outward act of charity or righteousness is hollow and unsustainable. Thus, the author emphasizes that compassion is the prerequisite for all true moral actions.
